CREATING DAY_NAME, MONTH_NAME, PROFIT_MARGIN

In [33]:
cursor = conn.cursor()

cursor.execute("""
ALTER TABLE Invoices
ADD DAY_NAME VARCHAR(20),
MONTH_NAME VARCHAR(20),
PROFIT_MARGIN DECIMAL(10, 2);
""")

conn.commit()
In [34]:
cursor.execute("""
UPDATE Invoices
SET 
DAY_NAME = DATENAME(WEEKDAY, OrderDate),
MONTH_NAME = DATENAME(MONTH, OrderDate),
PROFIT_MARGIN = Profit*100.0/NULLIF(Sales,.0);
""")
    
conn.commit()

SALES, PROFIT AND PROFIT MARGIN BY SEGMENT

In [42]:
pd.read_sql("""
SELECT C.Segment,
SUM(I.Sales) AS TOTAL_SALES,
SUM(I.Profit) AS TOTAL_PROFIT,
ROUND(SUM(I.Profit) * 100.0 / SUM(I.Sales),2) AS PROFIT_MARGIN
FROM customers AS C
INNER JOIN Invoices AS I
ON C.CustomerId = I.CustomerId
GROUP BY C.Segment
ORDER BY TOTAL_SALES DESC, TOTAL_PROFIT DESC;

""", engine)

SALES & PROFIT BY YEAR, MONTH_NAME, CATEGORY & SUB-CATEGORY

In [58]:
pd.read_sql("""
SELECT MONTH_NUM, MONTH_NAME, YEAR, Category, [Sub-Category], TOTAL_SALES, TOTAL_PROFIT
FROM (SELECT MONTH(I.OrderDate) AS MONTH_NUM, I.MONTH_NAME, YEAR(I.OrderDate) AS YEAR, P.Category, P.[Sub-Category],
SUM(I.Sales) AS TOTAL_SALES, SUM(I.Profit) AS TOTAL_PROFIT,
ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY YEAR(I.OrderDate), MONTH(I.OrderDate) ORDER BY SUM(I.Sales) DESC, SUM(I.Profit) DESC) AS RN
FROM Invoices AS I
INNER JOIN Products AS P ON P.ProductId = I.ProductId
GROUP BY MONTH(I.OrderDate), I.MONTH_NAME, YEAR(I.OrderDate), P.Category, P.[Sub-Category]) AS A
WHERE RN = 1
ORDER BY YEAR, MONTH_NUM;
""", engine)

TOP 3 PRODUCTS BY SALES WITHIN EACH CATEGORY

In [65]:
pd.read_sql("""
SELECT *
FROM (SELECT P.Category, P.[Sub-Category], P.ProductId, P.ProductName,
SUM(I.Sales)  AS TOTAL_SALES,
SUM(I.Profit) AS TOTAL_PROFIT,
RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY P.Category ORDER BY SUM(I.Sales) DESC) AS SALES_RANK
FROM Invoices AS I
INNER JOIN Products AS P ON P.ProductId = I.ProductId
GROUP BY P.Category, P.[Sub-Category], P.ProductId, P.ProductName) AS A
WHERE SALES_RANK <= 3
ORDER BY Category, SALES_RANK;
""", engine)

CONCLUSION¶

The analysis of the Iranian Cosmetics & Personal Care Sales dataset shows a total of ﷼18.84 billion in sales, ﷼4.85 billion in profit, and an overall profit margin of 25.73% across 14,586 invoices and 2,500 registered customers.

Customer sales are broadly distributed, with the top customer generating 26.4 million in sales. The three customer segments also show relatively similar performance, with Corporate generating the highest sales and profit, but only a small difference compared with Consumer and Home Office.

Among geographic locations, Tehran generated the highest sales and profit, while Qom generated the lowest. However, profit margins across locations are very similar, indicating that the difference is mainly related to sales volume rather than major differences in profitability.

For shipping methods, Same Day generated the highest sales and profit, while First Class generated the lowest sales. However, margins remain relatively stable across shipping methods.

At the weekly level, Friday generated the highest sales, while Wednesday generated the highest profit. Saturday recorded the lowest sales and profit. Monthly analysis showed July as the strongest month and April as the weakest month in 2025.

Product analysis shows that sales are widely distributed across the 500 products, with the top-selling product contributing less than 1% of total sales. However, inconsistencies between some product names and their assigned categories/sub-categories were identified, so category-level product insights should be interpreted with caution.

Overall, the dataset shows stable profitability across customers, segments, regions and shipping methods, while differences in performance are primarily driven by sales volume.

CONCLUSION¶

The analysis of the Iranian Cosmetics & Personal Care Sales dataset shows a total of ﷼18.84 billion in sales, ﷼4.85 billion in profit, and an overall profit margin of 25.73% across 14,586 invoices and 2,500 registered customers.

Customer sales are broadly distributed, with the top customer generating 26.4 million in sales. The three customer segments also show relatively similar performance, with Corporate generating the highest sales and profit, but only a small difference compared with Consumer and Home Office.

Among geographic locations, Tehran generated the highest sales and profit, while Qom generated the lowest. However, profit margins across locations are very similar, indicating that the difference is mainly related to sales volume rather than major differences in profitability.

For shipping methods, Same Day generated the highest sales and profit, while First Class generated the lowest sales. However, margins remain relatively stable across shipping methods.

At the weekly level, Friday generated the highest sales, while Wednesday generated the highest profit. Saturday recorded the lowest sales and profit. Monthly analysis showed July as the strongest month and April as the weakest month in 2025.

Product analysis shows that sales are widely distributed across the 500 products, with the top-selling product contributing less than 1% of total sales. However, inconsistencies between some product names and their assigned categories/sub-categories were identified, so category-level product insights should be interpreted with caution.

Overall, the dataset shows stable profitability across customers, segments, regions and shipping methods, while differences in performance are primarily driven by sales volume.
